text: Hello, I'm Didgee. This one's for you and your grown up. Snuggle up. Ready?
Before we start, let's do our big breath. Breathe in, and out.
Lovely.
Now, thinking caps on. Remember our last adventure? Some screen things are pretend.
So when we're not sure if something on a screen is real, what do we ask?
That's right. We ask, "Is this real?" Clever you.
Well, today we find something on the screen that is real. Very, very real.
Today we learn one big thing. The words you send on a screen land on a real person's feelings. So we choose kind words.
Say our special word. Kind. Just four little letters. K, I, N, D.
Look at this phone. The screen looks like glass, doesn't it? But here's a little secret.
It isn't glass at all. It's a window. And on the other side of the window, there's a real person.
A real friend with a real heart. A friend who giggles.
Who gets happy and sad and everything in between. Just like you.
Now watch what happens when you type a word. Hi.
The word doesn't stay on the glass. Oh no. It folds itself into a tiny paper plane
and it flies through the window all the way to the real person.
And it lands right on their feelings.
Kind words land warm, like a hug, like sunshine.
Now, one more true thing, because you're big enough to know it.
Most people on the other side of the window are kind. Most planes land warm.
But some people send unkind words, and some people pretend to be someone they are not.
A bit like dressing up, but not for fun.
If that ever happens, you don't have to fix it. You just tell your grown up.
Telling is never naughty, and it is never, ever your fault.
Pause me here. Grown up, ask your little one:
When someone says something kind to you, how does it feel in your tummy?
Have a little chat. I'll wait.
Here's how a chat like this can sound. A child might say, "I like it when my friend says well done."
And the grown up says, "Me too. It makes me feel happy right here."
And guess what? Your kind words do the same for other people, even through the screen.
You have a superpower. Every day you get to pick your words, little paper planes,
flying from your heart to somebody else's. So we pick the warm ones,
because a real person catches every single plane.
And here's the helper part. If someone on a screen is unkind to your friend, you can be the helper.
You don't join in. You tell a grown up, and you send your friend something extra kind.
So the warm planes outnumber the cold ones. Helpers are heroes.
Pause me again. Grown up, ask: who could we send a kind message to right now?
Pick one person you both love. I'll be right here.
So when we look at a screen, what do we remember?
Say it with me, three times. Big voices!
Real person on the other side.
Real person on the other side.
Real person on the other side.
And here's the little bit that goes with it. If someone is unkind, that is never your fault.
Go and tell.
Tonight, here's the fun bit. Together, send one kind message
To Granddad, to a cousin, to a friend.
It can be tiny. I love you. You are the best.
Or just a big smiley face.
Send it from your grown up's phone, snuggled up together. Then watch what happens.
Somewhere, a real person will smile,
because your kind word just flew through the window and landed right on their heart.
Before I go, show your grown up one thing you remember from today. Anything at all.
Got it? Brilliant.
And grown up, one kind message tonight.
Remember, screens are better together. See you next time.
